name: Chang'e 6 and Queqiao-2
short_status: Success: first-ever far-side sample return. 1,935.3 g landed in Inner Mongolia on Jun 25, 2024; Queqiao-2 relay still operating, sample science running hot through 2026.
tagline: CNSA · China · Sample return · 2024 · Commercial and multipolar Success
stats: far-side sample returned, the only far-side material on Earth
launch to touchdown in Inner Mongolia
measured age of the South Pole-Aitken basin
Queqiao-2 relay dish that made far-side comms possible

facts.label: Chang'e 6 launch
facts.value: 3 May 2024, 09:27 UTC (17:27 Beijing time), Long March 5 from Wenchang Space Launch Site, Hainan

facts.label: Lunar orbit insertion / ICUBE-Q deploy
facts.value: 8 May 2024: braked into lunar orbit and released Pakistan's ICUBE-Q cubesat (approx 7 kg, Pakistan's first lunar spacecraft; returned its first Moon images 11 May 2024)

facts.label: Landing
facts.value: 1 June 2024, 22:23 UTC (06:23 on 2 June, Beijing time), southern Apollo basin within the South Pole-Aitken basin

facts.label: Landing site coordinates
facts.value: 41.6385 S, 206.0148 E (equivalently 153.9852 W), elevation -5,256 m, horizontal accuracy plus or minus 30 m; lander sits on the rim of an eroded crater about 50 m across (LROC NAC M1472410644L, imaged 7 June 2024)

facts.label: Sample mass
facts.value: 1,935.3 g of far-side soil and rock (surface scoop plus subsurface drill), announced by CNSA on 28 June 2024; mission team described the material as more viscous and clumpier than earlier lunar samples

facts.label: First launch from the far side
facts.value: Ascender lifted off 4 June 2024, 07:38 Beijing time (3 June, 23:38 UTC), the first rocket launch ever from the Moon's far side

facts.label: Lunar-orbit docking and sample transfer
facts.value: 6 June 2024, 14:48 Beijing time: ascender docked with the orbiter-returner in a 210 km lunar orbit; sample container transferred to the returner by 15:24

facts.label: Return to Earth
facts.value: 25 June 2024: reentry capsule landed in Siziwang Banner, Inner Mongolia, 53 days after launch

facts.label: International payloads on the lander
facts.value: DORN radon-outgassing detector (France/CNES), NILS negative-ion detector (ESA, built in Sweden), INRRI passive laser retroreflector (Italy); ICUBE-Q cubesat (Pakistan) rode on the orbiter

facts.label: NILS result
facts.value: First-ever detection of negative ions at the lunar surface, and ESA's first scientific data collected on the Moon; instrument logged over three hours of data, three times the mission-success requirement

facts.label: Queqiao-2 launch
facts.value: 20 March 2024, 08:31 Beijing time (00:31 UTC), Long March 8 from Wenchang, with Tiandu-1 and Tiandu-2 comms/navigation tech-test smallsats as rideshares

facts.label: Queqiao-2 orbit and hardware
facts.value: Entered lunar orbit 24 March 2024; works from an elliptical frozen orbit of roughly 200 x 16,000 km at 62.4 deg inclination (24-hour period); 4.2 m parabolic dish for X-band/UHF links to surface craft, 0.6 m dish to Earth; design life 8 to 10 years; supports Chang'e 4, 6, 7 and 8

facts.label: Youngest dated far-side basalt
facts.value: 2.83 billion years (2807 plus or minus 3 Myr), radiometrically dated from Chang'e 6 basalt fragments, published in Science in November 2024; a separate 4.2-billion-year-old basalt clast records much earlier volcanism

facts.label: South Pole-Aitken basin age
facts.value: 4.25 billion years, dated from Chang'e 6 norite fragments (Chinese Academy of Sciences team, National Science Review, published March 2025), making SPA a sample-anchored calibration point for lunar chronology

facts.label: Far-side mantle water
facts.value: 1 to 1.5 micrograms of water per gram in the basalts' mantle source (Nature, April 2025), drier than nearside estimates and hinting at a hemispheric water dichotomy

facts.label: July 2025 Nature package
facts.value: Four Nature papers (9-10 July 2025) from CAS-led teams laid out far-side volcanism at 4.2 and 2.8 Ga, a lunar-dynamo rebound around 2.8 Ga, low mantle water, and a depleted mantle source, the first evolutionary history of the far side

facts.label: February 2026 chronology result
facts.value: Science Advances study (published 4 Feb 2026) using Chang'e 6 samples found near-side and far-side cratering rates essentially consistent, enabling a unified lunar chronology and offering no support for a Late Heavy Bombardment spike

timeline: Queqiao-2 relay satellite launches on a Long March 8 from Wenchang at 00:31 UTC, with Tiandu-1/2 rideshares
Queqiao-2 enters lunar orbit, settling into an elliptical frozen orbit (about 200 x 16,000 km, 24-hour period)
Chang'e 6 launches at 09:27 UTC on a Long March 5 from Wenchang
Lunar orbit insertion; Pakistan's ICUBE-Q cubesat deployed into lunar orbit
Lander touches down at 22:23 UTC in the southern Apollo basin, far side of the Moon
2 to 3 Jun 2024
Scoop and drill sampling; DORN and NILS run on the surface, with all comms via Queqiao-2
Ascender lifts off at 23:38 UTC, the first launch from the lunar far side
Ascender docks with the orbiter-returner in lunar orbit; sample container transferred
NASA's LRO photographs the lander on the rim of a 50 m crater; LROC later publishes site coordinates 41.6385 S, 206.0148 E
Reentry capsule lands in Siziwang Banner, Inner Mongolia; first far-side samples on Earth
CNSA announces the official sample mass: 1,935.3 g
Nov 2024
First headline science: 2.83-billion-year-old far-side basalt reported in Science and Nature
Mar 2025
South Pole-Aitken basin dated to 4.25 billion years from Chang'e 6 norites (National Science Review)
9 to 10 Jul 2025
Four-paper Nature package delivers the first evolutionary history of the Moon's far side
Science Advances chronology study: near/far-side impact rates match; no support for a Late Heavy Bombardment spike
Queqiao-2 stands by as relay for Chang'e 7, whose launch was postponed on 23 Aug 2026 with no new date announced (as of 2 Nov 2026)
